result.title: PaMIR: Open Benchmark of Public Credit-Default Datasets
result.summary: We release PaMIR (Public Arrival-ordered Measurement for Inference in Risk), an open benchmark for credit-default prediction when labels are scarce and arrive late. The field's reference benchmark studies use eight datasets each, only two or four of them public. PaMIR brings together 19 public datasets with binary default labels -- 1.24M loans, firms and card accounts from nine countries -- rebuilt from pinned source snapshots by one leakage-audited recipe and never redistributed; to our knowledge it is the one of its kind as of today. Every model is a single function, scored under a repeated i.i.d. split and a label-delayed stream in which each application is scored on arrival, with AUC reported by label budget; fleet means are withheld unless every dataset is scored. A synthetic-data harness tests generated training rows without letting a generator see held-out rows. This report describes release 0.4.0 of this living benchmark.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文发布 PaMIR，一个面向信用违约预测的开放基准，汇集 19 个公开数据集，并采用统一的防泄漏流程、重复 i.i.d. 划分与标签延迟流式评估，报告按标签预算的 AUC。
